Post-acquisition corrections are limited when biological variation is large, signals approach detection limits, or matrix effects are strong. We propose the TLQ method, consisting of Tandem Mixing, Linear Deduction, and Quantile Quality-Weighted Median. Tandem Mixing compresses between-group matrix differences and enhances low-abundance signals via equal-volume mixing of paired samples. Linear Deduction removes background and back-calculates the treatment signal, yielding a deduced fold change closer to the true treatment-to-control ratio. The third module performs robust screening using a quality-weighted median with Bootstrap confidence intervals. A candidates-of-interest mechanism improves coverage without compromising accuracy. The modules can be deployed flexibly (paired mode, P_R mode, or standalone third module). We also propose a general group-level diagnostic indicator (GDI) framework. GDI compares pooled and individual estimates and normalizes their discrepancy against a stochastic expectation, making systematic distortion quantifiable. GDI is platform-independent and serves as an independent reliability annotation layer in the TLQ method..
items.authors: Teng Teng, Yuchun Lu, Tonglei Qiao, Wei Feng, Chun-E Liu, Feng Liu

items.title: Reading the charge state of hydrogenated nanodiamonds: the 1330 cm-1 Fano feature as an interfacial probe
items.abstract: Hydrogenated nanodiamonds combine unusual electrokinetic charging with electronic properties that are highly sensitive to their surrounding environment, yet the relationship between molecular adsorption, interfacial charge and carrier state remains poorly understood. Here, a homologous series of anionic and cationic surfactants with C3–C16 alkyl chains is used as a controlled molecular perturbation of oxidized and hydrogenated detonation (DND) and high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) nanodiamonds. By combining ζ-potential measurements, FTIR spectroscopy and electrical transport, we examine how surfactant polarity and chain length affect these chemically and structurally distinct interfaces. Particular attention is given to the ~1330 cm-1 Fano-type infrared feature of HPHT H-ND, which we establish here as a spectroscopic probe of changes in its interfacial electronic state. The comparison reveals a marked contrast between the comparatively electrostatically hard H-DND interface and the electronically responsive HPHT H-ND surface, where molecular interactions can substantially modify the charge-transfer state. More broadly, the results show that molecular adsorption, electrokinetic charge and electronic carrier response need not evolve in parallel, supporting the Fano-type feature as a sensitive readout of molecularly regulated hydrogenated nanodiamond interfaces.
items.authors: Neha Sharma, Ondrej Szabo, Katerina Kolarova, Stepan Stehlik

items.title: From Metal-Organic Precursors to Coalesced Thin Films: A Predictive, End-to-End Atomistic Framework for MOCVD Multilayer TMD Growth
items.abstract: Metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) enables scalable synthesis of layered two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), yet the atomistic mechanisms linking precursor chemistry to multilayer nucleation and film evolution remain elusive, limiting synthesis control. Here, we establish a predictive mechanistic framework for multilayer TMD growth using MoS 2 as a representative system. Combining density functional theory, ReaxFF molecular dynamics, machine learning, and experimental validation, we reveal how metal antisites occupying chalcogen vacancies intrinsically form through surface interactions and serve as transient nucleation centers under experimentally relevant conditions. These defects stabilize epitaxial registry through covalent bonding and ultimately diffuse into the epilayer to form van der Waals interfaces. During this process, H 2 S vapor pressure influences metal-organic precursor decomposition by lowering the complete Mo(CO) 6 decomposition temperature, thereby promoting nucleation-center formation. This framework shifts layered-material synthesis from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive control, providing a computational route for growth of next-generation two-dimensional materials.
items.authors: Matin Salimi Irdmusa, Luca Donati, Fazil Safarov, Yu-Chuan Lin, Yun Kyung Shin, Surahit Chewle
items.title_zh: 从金属有机前驱体到合并薄膜：MOCVD多层TMD生长的预测性原子框架
items.summary_zh: 金属有机化学气相沉积（MOCVD）能够大规模合成层状二维半导体，如过渡金属二硫化物（TMDs），但前驱体化学与多层成核及薄膜演化之间的原子机制尚不明确，限制了合成控制。本文以MoS₂为代表系统，建立了多层TMD生长的预测性机制框架。通过结合密度泛函理论、ReaxFF分子动力学、机器学习和实验验证，我们揭示了金属反位点通过表面相互作用在实验相关条件下如何内在形成，并作为瞬态成核中心。这些缺陷通过共价键稳定外延对齐，最终扩散到外层形成范德瓦尔斯界面。在此过程中，H₂S蒸气压通过降低Mo(CO)₆的完全分解温度影响金属有机前驱体的分解，从而促进成核中心的形成。该框架将层状材料的合成从经验试错转向预测控制，为下一代二维材料的生长提供了计算路径。

items.title: Deciphering Ionic Conductivity Differences in Linear Carbonate Electrolytes: Conformational Shrinkage and Solvation Structure in Dimethyl vs Diethyl Carbonate
items.abstract: Dimethyl carbonate (DMC)-based electrolytes consistently show higher ionic conductivity than diethyl carbonate (DEC)-based ones despite their comparable viscosities and dielectric constants. Here, classical MD simulations with LiPF 6 as the salt are used to elucidate the molecular origins of this difference. LiPF 6 -DMC electrolytes contain a larger population of solvent-separated ion pairs (SSIPs), whereas LiPF 6 -DEC electrolytes exhibit a higher population of ion aggregates (AGGs). Among various species, SSIPs make the dominant contribution to ionic conductivity, accounting for the higher conductivity of DMC-based electrolytes. Both solvents exist predominantly in two conformations, cis-cis (CC) and cis-trans (CT), defined by the torsional angle about the C-O bond; the former is largely non-polar, while the latter has a substantial dipole moment of nearly 4 D. In both electrolytes, the CT fraction increases with salt concentration, consistent with the stronger ion-dipole interactions of the CT conformer with ions and the fractions are comparable for DMC and DEC. Nevertheless, DMC retains a larger fraction of lithium ions as SSIPs. Although CT-DMC and CT-DEC have nearly identical polarities, more CT-DMC molecules coordinate Li + than CT-DEC molecules do. This difference arises from their distinct conformational sizes: CT-DMC has a volume approximately 8% smaller than that of CC-DMC, whereas the corresponding decrease for DEC is only about 2%. The smaller relative size of CT-DMC permits more of it to coordinate Li + to yield effective electrostatic shielding. This, in turn, leads to a larger SSIP population and higher ionic conductivity of LiPF 6 -DMC relative to LiPF 6 -DEC.
items.authors: Mansi Jain, Sundaram Balasubramanian
items.title_zh: 解析线性碳酸盐电解质中离子导电性差异
items.summary_zh: 尽管二甲基碳酸酯（DMC）和二乙基碳酸酯（DEC）在粘度和介电常数上相似，但基于DMC的电解质表现出更高的离子导电性。本文通过经典分子动力学模拟，使用LiPF6作为盐，探讨了这一差异的分子起源。LiPF6-DMC电解质中溶剂分离离子对（SSIPs）的数量较多，而LiPF6-DEC电解质中离子聚集体（AGGs）的数量较高。SSIPs对离子导电性贡献最大，解释了DMC电解质的高导电性。两种溶剂主要存在于顺-顺（CC）和顺-反（CT）两种构象中，前者几乎是非极性的，后者具有接近4 D的显著偶极矩。随着盐浓度的增加，CT构象的比例在两种电解质中均有所增加，但DMC中保留的锂离子作为SSIPs的比例更大。尽管CT-DMC和CT-DEC的极性几乎相同，但CT-DMC分子对Li+的配位能力更强，这源于它们不同的构象尺寸。

items.title: Charge-Encoded Anion Sublattices Drive Ordering and Phase Selection in Layered Chalcogenides
items.abstract: Predicting the sites where anions order in a crystal, and when that ordering drives structural rearrangement, remains a challenge in mixed-anion chemistry. Here we show that both are linked to the distribution of charge on the anion sublattice of ACuMIVQ3 chalcogenides. Bader analysis of four competing polymorphs reveals that the sequencing of polyhedra controls the range of charge across anion sites (Δq) and programs each structure with a distinct charge-encoded anion sublattice. Thirteen new mixedchalcogen compounds were prepared, and the anion site occupancies were determined through single crystal X-ray diffraction. While sulfoselenides tend to adopt structures with small Δq, where they form near-ideal solid solutions, greater anion disparity in the selenotellurides and sulfotellurides leads to enhanced ordering, which drives formation of alternate structures with higher Δq. These structures provide terraced charge landscapes with more strongly differentiated sites, suggesting that structure selection depends on how well the anion sublattice matches the chemical disparity of the anion mixture. This trend culminates in KCuZrTeSeS, where S, Se, and Te order across three distinct sites in the Pnma structure, a phase not adopted by any single-anion end member, and the first demonstration of site-selective ordering of all three chalcogens in a single material. An enrichment factor connecting site occupancy with Bader charge further shows that the most electronegative chalcogen in a given mixture preferentially occupies the highest-charge site. Together, the results establish charge-encoded anion sublattices as a framework for predicting anion ordering and phase selection in extended solids.
items.authors: Ayat Tassanov, Huiju Lee, Keela K. Zambre, Pedro R. Trinidad-Pérez, Yi Xia, James M Hodges

items.title: Geminal Metalloid Substituents Enable Stereoselective Geometric Isomerization of Highly Substituted Alkenes via Energy-Transfer Catalysis
items.abstract: Controlling alkene geometry with high stereochemical precision remains a fundamental challenge in synthetic chemistry, particularly for highly substituted systems. Here we report a stereoselective photoisomerization of gem-diborylalkenes in which visible light enables efficient E→Z interconversion of geminal metalloids-substituted carbon–carbon double bonds through a triplet energy-transfer (EnT) mechanism, overcoming the long-standing limitation of stereoselective photoisomerization of highly (tetra)substituted alkenes. A broad range of tri- and tetra-substituted alkenes are converted to the thermodynamically less stable Z-isomer with up to 99:1 selectivity. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that stereocontrol arises from both interplay between excited-state deconjugation due to steric bulkiness and substratephotocatalyst interactions. Sequential functionalizations of both geometrically defined diborylalkene isomers are also demonstrated, enabling the stereodivergent construction of complex stereodefined alkenes. Beyond facilitating stereoselective geometric isomerization of tri- and tetrasubstituted alkenes, this work establishes (gem)-dimetalloid alkenes as light-programmable scaffolds and introduces a general strategy for boron-mediated photochemical control of alkene stereochemistry with implications for molecular and materials design.
items.authors: Nadim Eghbarieh, Nicole Hanania, Brandon E. Haines, Ahmad Masarwa
items.title_zh: 双金属取代烯烃的立体选择性几何异构化研究
items.summary_zh: 控制高立体化学精度的烯烃几何形状仍然是合成化学中的一项基本挑战，尤其是对于高度取代的体系。本文报道了一种双硼烯的立体选择性光异构化，其中可见光通过三重态能量转移机制实现了双金属取代的碳-碳双键的高效E→Z互变，克服了高度（四）取代烯烃的立体选择性光异构化的长期限制。多种三取代和四取代烯烃被转化为热力学上不太稳定的Z-异构体，选择性高达99:1。机理研究和密度泛函理论（DFT）计算表明，立体控制源于由于立体庞大而导致的激发态去共轭与底物-光催化剂相互作用之间的相互作用。此外，本文还展示了几何定义的双硼烯异构体的顺序功能化，促进了复杂立体定义烯烃的立体分歧构建。此研究不仅促进了三取代和四取代烯烃的立体选择性几何异构化，还确立了（双）金属取代烯烃作为光编程支架的应用，提出了一种用于硼介导的烯烃立体化学光控制的通用策略。

items.title: Heterogeneous Catalysts as Electrochemical Cells: Completing the Circuit using Proton Buffers in Nonaqueous Media
items.abstract: Thermochemical redox reactions with heterogeneous catalysts often proceed by an "electrochemical" mechanism that features coupled redox half-reactions. Studies supporting this mechanism have typically been performed with water as the solvent; however, many organic oxidation reactions feature non-aqueous solvent. Here, we analyze the aerobic oxidation of hydroquinone with iron-containing nitrogen-doped carbon (Fe-N-C) catalysts in acetonitrile. Addition of proton buffers significantly accelerates the reaction, and mechanistic data indicate the buffers support proton transfer between the two redox half-reactions, proton-coupled oxidation of the hydroquinone and O2 reduction, which take place at different active sites on the catalyst surface. Kinetic studies of the thermochemical aerobic oxidation reaction are complemented by electrochemical studies, including linear-sweep voltametric analysis of both independent half-reactions. Collectively, the data provide a selfconsistent mechanistic picture that highlights the importance of proton management in supporting thermal heterogeneous catalytic redox reactions in non-aqueous solvent.
items.authors: Patrick Q. Kelly, Woonjin Jang, Ian J. Garvey, James B. Gerken, Shannon S. Stahl

items.title: GCCDDCs Enable Tumor-Selective Lysosomal Degradation and Payload Delivery via GC-C-Mediated Trafficking
items.abstract: Degrader–drug conjugates (DDCs) represent an emerging class of therapeutic agents that integrate the mechanism of targeted protein degradation with enhanced drug delivery, offering a promising strategy for precision cancer therapy. We herein report the rational design of GC-C–targeted degrader–drug conjugates (GCCDDCs), a bifunctional modality that promotes selective PD-L1 degradation while concurrently delivering a cytotoxic payload to GC-C–expressing cancer cells. Utilizing the GC-C agonist linaclotide as a targeting moiety, we first engineered GC-C–mediated lysosome-targeting chimeras (GCCTACs), which effectively induced degradation of both extracellular and membranebound proteins in a selective manner. By conjugating a PD-L1-targeting degrader to the microtubule-disrupting agent MMAE, the resulting GCCDDCs exhibit potent antitumor efficacy through coordinated immune checkpoint degradation and direct cytotoxicity. The development of GCCDDCs expands the pharmacological toolbox for targeted protein degraders (TPDs) and X–drug conjugates (XDCs), thereby offering broad utility in chemical
items.authors: Yi Zhou, Tengfei Liu, Huaihuai Shi, Xiaozhuo Tan, Hui Pan, Wenyan Dong

items.title: An Ab Initio-Kinetic Framework for Predicting Electrochemical Passivation of Materials
items.abstract: Recent years have seen a strong push towards data-driven discovery of materials in many areas, from structural alloys to energy devices to quantum materials. However, many applications involve prolonged exposure to aqueous and/or acidic electrochemical conditions that can promote material degradation. Despite the critical role of stability in determining material performance, there is a lack of models that are capable of predicting a material’s corrosion-passivation behavior without relying on empirical parameters or fitting. In this work, we address this gap by developing an ab initio kinetic model (AKM), which integrates an existing empirical passivation growth theory, the Point Defect Model (PDM), into a non-empirical first principles-based framework. We redefine the five primary inputs of the PDM, previously ad hoc or experimentally-fitted, into ab initio -calculable parameters, entirely removing their empirical dependence. We then apply AKM to predict the passivation growth of six common metal-film systems. In comparison to experiments reported in the literature, we obtain a strong qualitative trend and reproduce the correct orders of magnitude, without any a priori experimental inputs. We further investigate passive-film formation in the Cu-CuO x system through a detailed computational case study, establishing guidelines for selecting appropriate surface terminations, oxygen vacancy configurations, and point defect concentrations. Sensitivity analyses further reveal that, within the PDM framework, the electrical driving force has a greater influence on passive-film growth than the chemical driving force. This work represents a vital step towards the development of high-throughput predictive modeling of materials’ electrochemical stability in applications where materials are exposed to aqueous media.
items.authors: Rachel Gorelik, Arunima K. Singh
items.title_zh: 基于从头算动力学的材料电化学钝化预测框架
items.summary_zh: 近年来，材料的基于数据的发现受到广泛关注，尤其是在结构合金、能源设备和量子材料等领域。然而，许多应用涉及在水性和/或酸性电化学条件下的长期暴露，这可能导致材料降解。尽管稳定性在材料性能中至关重要，但缺乏能够预测材料腐蚀-钝化行为的模型，而不依赖于经验参数或拟合。本研究开发了一种从头算动力学模型（AKM），将现有的经验钝化生长理论——点缺陷模型（PDM）整合到非经验的第一性原理框架中。我们将PDM的五个主要输入重新定义为从头算可计算的参数，完全消除了其经验依赖性。通过AKM，我们预测了六种常见金属薄膜系统的钝化生长，与文献中的实验结果相比，获得了强烈的定性趋势，并重现了正确的数量级，而无需任何先验实验输入。我们进一步通过详细的计算案例研究探讨了Cu-CuO x系统中的钝化膜形成，为选择适当的表面终止提供了指导。

items.title: Optimizing mechanical properties and ionic conductivity of hybrid hydrogel electrolytes for flexible zinc-ion batteries
items.abstract: Wearable electronics require energy storage systems that combine mechanical flexibility, safety, and electrochemical performance, making aqueous zinc-ion batteries using hydrogel polymer electrolytes (HPEs) a promising approach. However, achieving hydrogels with both high mechanical toughness and ionic conductivity remains a major challenge. Herein, a zwitterionic poly(sulfobetaine methylacrylate)-tetraethylene glycol dimethacrylate (PSBMA-EG) hydrogel was combined with a silica network to form an organic/inorganic hybrid electrolyte. The results demonstrated the successful synthesis and cross-linking of the organic and inorganic networks using 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate (TMSPMA) as a coupling agent. The acrylate-to-silica ratio (Ac:Si), as the composition-dependency, was varied to investigate its effect on the morphology, swelling behaviour, and glass transition temperature of the obtained hydrogels. Typically, increasing the Ac:Si ratio resulted in more homogeneous and porous structures with higher water uptake. The mechanical and electrochemical properties were evaluated using uniaxial compression and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), respectively. The HPE with the optimized combination of properties was obtained at an Ac:Si ratio of 2:1, exhibiting a toughness of 152.41 ± 30.12 kJ m –3 and an ionic conductivity of 118.01 ± 28.04 mS cm –1 .
items.authors: Iben Edelbo Lauritzen, Jonas Klarskov Nielsen, Patrick Ullits Pilgaard, Phillip Dyran, Hanne Colding Bundgaard, Mikkel Vinkler Kristensen
items.title_zh: 优化混合水凝胶电解质的机械性能和离子导电性用于柔性锌离子电池
items.summary_zh: 可穿戴电子设备需要结合机械灵活性、安全性和电化学性能的能量存储系统，因此使用水性锌离子电池和水凝胶聚合物电解质（HPEs）是一种有前景的方法。然而，实现高机械韧性和离子导电性的水凝胶仍然是一个主要挑战。本文将两性离子聚（磺基甜菜碱甲基丙烯酸酯）-四乙烯乙二醇二甲基丙烯酸酯（PSBMA-EG）水凝胶与二氧化硅网络结合，形成有机/无机混合电解质。结果表明，使用3-(三甲氧基硅烷)丙基甲基丙烯酸酯（TMSPMA）作为偶联剂成功合成并交联了有机和无机网络。通过改变丙烯酸酯与二氧化硅的比例（Ac:Si），研究其对水凝胶形态、膨胀行为和玻璃转变温度的影响。通常，增加Ac:Si比例会导致更均匀和多孔的结构，水分吸收量更高。通过单轴压缩和电化学阻抗谱（EIS）评估了机械和电化学性能。优化的HPE在Ac:Si比例为2:1时获得，表现出152.41 ± 30.12 kJ m –3的韧性和118.01 ± 28.04 mS cm –1的离子导电性。

items.title: Three-dimensional fluorescence lifetime imaging of a molecular rotor at complex interfaces of grease
items.abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) maps local physicochemical properties on a confocal laser-scanning microscope. Soft materials are a promising target for FLIM, given their demand for multi-scale microanalysis; of particular interest are the interfacial properties of complex fluids, which remain underexplored. Here, we demonstrate three-dimensional FLIM mapping at complex interfaces of grease as a model system. In grease, tens-of-nanometer-scale thickener fibers form a three-dimensional network in the base oil, and the extent to which fiber–oil interactions alter the local oil properties is an open question. Our bulk measurements confirm that the fluorescence lifetime of a molecular-rotor dye dissolved in the oil is coupled to the local viscosity. Three-dimensional FLIM reveals that the lifetime of the molecular rotor significantly increases at the fiber–oil interfaces. Phasor analysis and pixel-level fitting show that the interfacial state arrests the rotation of the molecular rotor, so the interface is solid-like rather than viscous. Its physicochemical origin may offer a new handle for designing grease materials. Beyond the ~200 nm resolution of our images, the lifetime-domain separation of the two states resolves their coexistence within a single diffraction-limited voxel. Three-dimensional high-resolution FLIM will broaden the mapping of interfacial properties in soft complex materials.
items.authors: Hideyo Tsurusawa, Ryo Shibata, Masaki Watanabe, Minami Soma, Takashi Nogi
items.title_zh: 三维荧光寿命成像研究润滑脂复杂界面分子转子的特性
items.summary_zh: 荧光寿命成像显微镜（FLIM）能够在共聚焦激光扫描显微镜上绘制局部物理化学特性。软材料是FLIM的一个重要研究对象，尤其是复杂流体的界面特性尚未得到充分探索。本文以润滑脂为模型系统，展示了在其复杂界面上进行三维FLIM映射的结果。在润滑脂中，纳米级增稠剂纤维在基础油中形成三维网络，纤维与油的相互作用如何改变局部油的性质仍然是一个未解之谜。我们的整体测量确认，溶解在油中的分子转子染料的荧光寿命与局部粘度相关。三维FLIM显示，分子转子在纤维-油界面处的寿命显著增加。相位分析和像素级拟合表明，界面状态抑制了分子转子的旋转，使得界面呈现固态特征而非粘性。其物理化学起源可能为润滑脂材料的设计提供新的思路。

items.title: Chemical tuning of framework libration as a design principle for Na-oxide superionic conductors
items.abstract: Most design principles for superionic conductors (SICs) are derived from known SICs and evaluated on static structures, which can miss transport enabled by finite-temperature framework motion. Both limitations are particularly severe for Na-oxides, a low-cost, stable chemistry with only a few known SIC frameworks. Here we establish a Na-oxide design principle that links local Na-site geometry to framework dynamics using chemical substitution and compositional modification strategies. Using molecular dynamics simulations with a Na-oxide-specialized machine-learning interatomic potential, we screen all 8,504 Na-oxides in the Materials Project and identify six superionic frameworks, four of them previously unreported. The highest extrapolated room-temperature conductivity reaches 29 mS cm -1 . We identify a finite-temperature Na-site size window of 1.2–1.5 Å that favors Na hopping and show that the framework motion required to access this window depends on the initial geometry: larger-amplitude libration opens initially small sites, whereas smaller-amplitude libration preserves initially larger sites. Thus, stronger framework motion is not universally favorable for ion transport. Furthermore, we show that libration is governed by polyhedral connectivity and can be tuned through Na content and cation substitution within a fixed framework. Our findings extend Na-oxide design principles from static structure to framework dynamics and indicate that frameworks overlooked at their default compositions can become conductive once the framework dynamics are tuned.
items.authors: Hyeon-Jong Lee, Jae-Seung Kim, You-Yeob Song, Minjun Kwon, Seungyong Shin, Jiwon Seo

items.title: Photochemical CO Evolution in a Quinone-Based Electrochemical CO2 Capture System
items.abstract: Quinone-based electrochemical CO2 capture in aprotic organic solvents relies on the redox-controlled formation of quinone–CO2 adducts. Understanding how these bound species respond to light is essential for identifying competing reaction pathways that may alter carrier stability and the chemical outcome of capture. Here, we investigate the photochemical behavior of electrochemically reduced 9,10-phenanthrenequinone (PAQ) in DMSO under CO2 and N2 using visible-light irradiation (440 nm). Electrochemical and spectroscopic measurements reveal light-responsive behavior of the reduced-PAQ/CO2 system. CO evolution is observed during irradiation under CO2, with earlier quantifiable detection and greater accumulation than under N2. Water addition strongly suppresses CO evolution, suggesting that water-induced changes in reduced-PAQ speciation affect the CO-forming pathway. Together, these observations suggest that reduced-PAQ speciation influences CO formation, with light-induced transformation of PAQ–CO2-bound species as a plausible contributing pathway. These findings highlight photochemical stability and waterdependent speciation as important considerations in the design of quinone-based CO2-capture systems.
items.authors: Hyung Chan Lim, Hyowon Seo

items.title: Continuous Solar-Adaptive Electrochemical Stripping for Circular Nitrogen Recovery from Urine
items.abstract: Solar electrochemical stripping (ECS) is a low-carbon circular economy approach to recover ammonia from wastewater that faces challenges in scale up and intermittent energy supply management. We present a novel autonomous solar-adaptive multistage ECS system that removed 94% of nitrogen from a continuous flow of influent urine and recovered 75% of nitrogen as ammonium sulfate fertilizer in over 80 hours of off-grid operation. To control urine flow rate, we identified a load ratio that maximizes nitrogen extraction across fluctuating solar power inputs. The first demonstrated multistage electrode stack configuration of ECS increased the system’s volumetric urine treatment capacity by 2.7x and revealed that hydraulic coupling of stages in series can increase nitrogen removal by 16.5% compared to parallel operation for the same urine flow rate and energy efficiency. Using these findings, ECS was operated as a three-stage configuration in real sunlight on two sunny days and one partially cloudy day, allowing current density to range from 4.7 mA/cm2 to 10.4 mA/cm2 proportionally to incident sunlight. Urine flow varied accordingly from 0.82 L/day to 1.92 L/day. Even as input power fluctuated, the system achieved consistent nitrogen extraction that varied less than 7% at steady state. This solar-adaptive (i.e., flexible) operation scheme would require 55% less battery storage than an equivalent constant operation scheme. Ultimately, this work elucidates a pathway to valorize alternative sources of ammonia nitrogen at the water-energy nexus, leverages demand-side response to support electrical grid stability, and reduces the need for renewable energy battery storage.
items.authors: Orisa Coombs, O. Godson Osele, William A. Tarpeh
items.title_zh: 连续太阳能自适应电化学剥离尿液中的氮回收
items.summary_zh: 太阳能电化学剥离（ECS）是一种低碳循环经济方法，用于从废水中回收氨，但在规模化和间歇性能源管理方面面临挑战。我们提出了一种新型自主太阳能自适应多级ECS系统，该系统在超过80小时的离网运行中，从连续流入的尿液中去除了94%的氮，并回收了75%的氮作为硫酸铵肥料。为控制尿液流量，我们确定了一个负载比，以最大化在波动的太阳能输入下的氮提取。首次展示的多级电极堆配置使系统的尿液处理能力提高了2.7倍，并显示串联阶段的水力耦合相比并联操作在相同尿液流量和能效下可提高16.5%的氮去除率。在两个晴天和一个部分多云的日子里，ECS以三级配置在真实阳光下运行，电流密度在4.7 mA/cm²到10.4 mA/cm²之间变化，尿液流量相应变化为0.82 L/day到1.92 L/day。尽管输入功率波动，系统在稳态下实现了一致的氮提取，变化幅度小于7%。这种太阳能自适应操作方案所需的电池储存量比传统方法减少了55%。

items.title: Signal Additivity as a Practical Criterion for Validating Kd Determination: Reconciling Conflicting Backscattering Interferometry Results
items.abstract: Backscattering interferometry (BSI) enables label-free, immobilization-free detection of molecular interactions in free solution, but published studies report conflicting outcomes, including saturable, nonsaturating, and poorly reproducible responses. Here, we develop a signal-additivity framework that distinguishes interaction detection from determination of the thermodynamic equilibrium dissociation constant, K d , and provides a basis for reconciling these reports. For a two-state system at fixed total target concentration, quantitative K d analysis requires the final referenced and control-subtracted response to be an affine function of equilibrium complex concentration over the fitted range. A general refractive-index expansion shows that nonlinear self-and crosscomponent contributions can survive control subtraction and generate composition-dependent residual signals. Illustrative simulations with a known input value, K d,true , show that such residuals can produce smooth, apparently saturable curves with biased apparent dissociation constants, K d,app , or strong concentration-range dependence of K d,app . Concentration-design analysis further illustrates, for a specified ligand-dependent residual model, a trade-off between upper-isotherm coverage and high-concentration residuals. Reinterpretation of representative BSI studies indicates that specificity, reproducibility, and apparent saturation support interaction detection but do not independently establish signal additivity. We therefore propose a workflow based on matched controls, concentration-range analysis, residual inspection, parameter-stability assessment, and binding-model evaluation, with measurements at different target concentrations when feasible. Although developed here using BSI, the underlying criterion applies more broadly to affinity studies in which a processed response is assumed to report equilibrium binding populations. BSI-derived values should be reported as K d,app unless signal additivity, adequate isotherm coverage, concentration accuracy, and binding-model adequacy are independently supported.
items.authors: Xingzhi Che, Alexander MacLellan, Ayesha Maqsood, Elyaa AlSafadi, Tong Ye Wang, Sergey N. Krylov
items.title_zh: 信号可加性作为Kd测定验证的实用标准
items.summary_zh: 背散射干涉仪（BSI）实现了无标签、无固定化的分子相互作用检测，但已有研究结果存在冲突，包括可饱和、不可饱和及重现性差的反应。本文提出了一种信号可加性框架，区分相互作用检测与热力学平衡解离常数Kd的测定，为调和这些报告提供基础。在固定总靶标浓度的双态系统中，定量Kd分析要求最终参考和控制减去的反应在拟合范围内是平衡复合物浓度的仿射函数。一般的折射率展开表明，非线性自我和交叉成分的贡献在控制减去后仍可存活，并产生依赖于组成的残余信号。已知输入值Kd,true的模拟显示，这些残余可以产生平滑、明显可饱和的曲线，并导致偏倚的表观解离常数Kd,app或Kd,app的强浓度范围依赖性。浓度设计分析进一步说明，在特定配体依赖的残余模型下，上等温线覆盖与高浓度残余之间存在权衡。对代表性BSI研究的重新解读表明，特异性和重现性。

items.title: Aminomutase-Inspired Methylene Insertion for α-to-β Homologative Transposition of Amino Acids
items.abstract: A versatile method for the preparation of synthetically valuable β2-homologated amino acid esters from simple α-amino acid esters is described. Inspired by pyridoxal 5′-phosphate-dependent aminomutase enzymes, the described strategy exploits a straightforward protocol for substrate activation, alkylation, and migration leveraging a bio-inspired 3-exo-trig radical cascade. This approach enables a novel homologative strategy towards β-amino acids via methylene insertion into the Cα–N bond of α-amino acids. A broad substrate scope is demonstrated, and key activator electronic factors are elucidated through experimental and computational mechanistic studies. By engaging α-amino acids directly, the method provides unique access to β2-homologated amino acids.
items.authors: Ayah W. Fidama, Vincent Huang, Yetong Lin, Jaclyn N. Mauro, Ethan T. A. Raffman, Jialin Li

items.title: Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC
items.abstract: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing the domain to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC. The present paper highlights further limitations of GCxGC: inadequate operation burdened with shortcomings are presented via examples taken from GCxGC literature; crowning the list with the inability to meet fundamental requirement that if a compound can be analyzed by 1D-GC it must remain analyzable by MDGC. The repertoire of the intertwining issues, each of which unavoidably rigs or even hamstrings the others, highlights that GCxGC has a built-in self-limiting feature. Attempts to overcome confinements via loosening the binding conditions turned GCxGC back to the form it emerged from decades ago, yet without getting rid of the hampering curbs. The unfavorable overall picture forces to consider viabilities of other concepts, with focus on avoiding errors and pitfalls of GCxGC while fulfilling basic requirements of MDGC. In our view, there are two alternatives. One is ZGC, principle of which was introduced in 1989, requirements and potential of which are presented here in more detail; the other is a concept called Quantum-GC, which is presented as an introductory approach.
items.authors: Endre Fuggerth

items.title: Conjugated Helicene Oligomers Displaying an Odd-Even Conformational and Aggregation Effect
items.abstract: Helicenes attract attention due to their spring-shaped structures and conjugated backbones. Synthesizing longer helicenes allows for structure-property relationship investigation as additional coil layers are achieved. Therefore, developing helicenes as building blocks for oligomers and polymers will increase understanding of property tuning upon chain extension. We report the synthesis of discrete oligomers using the helicene N[5]HDI from lengths n=1 to n=5. Selective bromination of the oligomers allows for extension to longer oligomers, as well as the potential to use them as monomer units in polymerizations. The oligomers exhibit an odd-even effect, where odd oligomers prefer a ‘coiled’ conformation, while even oligomers prefer a ‘snake’ conformation. This results in improved orbital overlap and effective conjugation in odd oligomers, and small changes in electronics but increased aggregation in even oligomers. The synthesis and structure-property tuning of N[5]HDI oligomers is an important step toward incorporating helicenes into polymers with enhanced mechanical and electronic properties.
items.authors: Rachael K. Mow, Zhenan Bao
items.title_zh: 奇偶效应的共轭螺旋烯寡聚物研究
items.summary_zh: 螺旋烯因其弹簧状结构和共轭骨架而受到关注。合成更长的螺旋烯有助于研究结构与性质之间的关系。本文合成了从n=1到n=5的螺旋烯N[5]HDI的离散寡聚物。通过选择性溴化，延长了寡聚物的链长，并可作为聚合反应中的单体单元。研究发现，奇数寡聚物倾向于“卷曲”构象，而偶数寡聚物则偏好“蛇形”构象。这导致奇数寡聚物的轨道重叠和有效共轭增强，而偶数寡聚物的电子性质变化较小但聚集性增强。N[5]HDI寡聚物的合成及其结构-性质调控是将螺旋烯引入具有增强机械和电子性能的聚合物的重要一步。

items.title: First-Principles Magnetic Anisotropy and Statistical-Mechanical Prediction of Magnetic Alignment in Aromatic PET-Type Polymer Domains
items.abstract: Gauge-including-atomic-orbital (GIAO) density functional theory calculations at the B3LYP/6-31+G(d,p) level are used to determine the molecular magnetic susceptibility tensors of a hydroxyl-terminated poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) oligomer series - PET1/BHET, PET2, and PET3 - and the results are carried through an explicit statistical-mechanical model of field-induced domain alignment. The isotropic molecular response becomes increasingly negative with oligomer length, while the chemically defined axial anisotropy along the terephthalate backbone remains approximately constant at 15–16 atomic units, showing that total diamagnetic response and magnetic anisotropy are governed by distinct structural features. A continuum orientational model based on the ratio λ = VΔχB2/(2μ0kBT) of magnetic to thermal energy is used to obtain the exact Boltzmann orientational distribution and the second-rank order parameter S, together with an overdamped-rotation estimate of the characteristic alignment time. Because a molecular susceptibility tensor is not automatically a bulk volume susceptibility, the continuum values reported here are explicitly identified as provisional, density-based phenomenological estimates rather than validated bulk quantities. The central physical result is that the coherently rotating domain volume, through its cubic scaling of the magnetic energy, dominates the alignment behaviour far more strongly than the modest variation in molecular anisotropy across the oligomer series, so that the crossover field for a given domain scales as B ∝ a-3⁄2. The framework separates a complete first-principles molecular-response and statistical-mechanics treatment from a deliberately provisional molecular-to-bulk conversion, and it identifies the specific calculations — conformer sampling, a structural-axis re-analysis for PET3, a method-sensitivity benchmark, and a validated coarse-graining scheme — required before the predicted alignment fields and order parameters can be compared quantitatively with experiment.
items.authors: Dibakar Roy

items.title: Nitrogen basicity dictates Fe-N-C-catalyzed aerobic oxidation activity
items.abstract: Iron-metalated nitrogen-doped carbon (Fe-N-C) materials rival platinum-based electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in fuel cells, and O2 reduction is proposed to occur at atomically dispersed Fe atoms coordinated by nitrogen within the graphitic material (FeNx). In recent years, similar catalysts have been shown to be effective for aerobic oxidation of organic substrates, often under non-aqueous conditions that are very different from electrocatalytic ORR conditions. Such reactions have been the focus of limited mechanistic attention, and little is known about the active sites and/or catalyst features that contribute to improved activity. Here, we investigate Fe-NC-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of hydroquinone to benzoquinone and two other organic reactions. The FeNx site density is found to have little influence over catalytic activity. Instead, we find that the basicity of nitrogen atoms in the Fe-N-C surface is the dominant feature that correlates with catalytic activity, with diagnostic insights gained from binding isotherm measurements with pivalic acid. Fe-N-C catalytic activity is shown to correlate directly with the pivalic acid binding constant (Kads) across a series of different catalysts. These insights provide a valuable foundation for future development and optimization of improved aerobic oxidation catalysts.
items.authors: Jesse J. Martinez, Ian J. Garvey, Woonjin Jang, Patrick Q. Kelly, Evelyn M. Widmaier, Melissa N. Hall

items.title: Target-Specific De Novo Drug Design via Fine-Tuned Language Models and Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulation Validation
items.abstract: De novo drug design remains an expensive and low-yield process, particularly for targets with limited bioactivity data. In this study, we fine-tuned the Qwen 2.5 0.5B model to treat ligand design as a sequence-to-sequence task from protein amino acid sequences to molecular SELFIES representations. A curated and balanced dataset derived from ChEMBL was used to reduce target-level data imbalance, followed by systematic evaluation using beam search and stochastic sampling. The fine-tuned model demonstrated strong ligand generation capability across multiple targets, achieving high validity, uniqueness, and novelty. Comparative analysis revealed that beam search favored conservative exploitation of learned chemical space, whereas sampling enabled broader exploration and higher novelty. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations for representative targets showed that generated compounds formed stable complexes with energetically favorable binding profiles comparable to known inhibitors. Notably, target-specific fine-tuning under extreme low data conditions, enabled through molecular representation augmentation, successfully guided ligand generation toward relevant structural frameworks. Our work suggests that small language models can be effectively fine-tuned for structure-aware, target-specific ligand design, even under limited bioactivity information.
items.authors: Phuong Nguyen

items.title: Nanocraft: Nanocrystal Assembly and Functionalization Toolkit
items.abstract: Nanoparticles find broad applications in optoelectronics, catalysis, and nanomedicine. While machinelearning and computational screening can accelerate their design, the structural chemical space of these materials remains underrepresented in current databases. Obtaining realistic atomistic models requires the proper representation of both the inorganic core and its surface chemistry, which are commonly treated through disjoint workflows relying on separate tools. We present Nanocraft, an open source Python toolkit for the generation and functionalization of nanocrystals and nanoparticles. Operating locally through an accessible Jupyter Notebook interface, Nanocraft does not require advanced coding skills and enables the rapid generation and manipulation of large datasets by varying core stoichiometries, shapes, ligand types and surface coverage. The toolkit provides automated surface passivation based on local oxidation states and enables facet selective ligand attachment within a single framework. Its structure generation pipeline accepts crystallographic CIF files or XYZ supercells and exports the resulting structures in XYZ format for direct use in molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and machine-learning workflows. We demonstrate Nanocraft’s capabilities by constructing a dataset of thiolcapped CdSe quantum dots. Both Nanocraft and the supporting information, including a User Guide, are available at https://github.com/jgrll/Nanocraft/.
items.authors: Justin Grill, Dominik Domin, Christophe Humbert, Carine Clavaguéra

items.title: Glucose Dehydrogenase Engineered for the Noncanonical Coenzyme NMN Outperforms Its Natural NAD-Dependent Activity
items.abstract: Engineering redox enzymes to utilize noncanonical coenzymes is critical for advancing in vitro enzymatic biocatalysis and in vivo bioorthogonal chemistry. However, engineered NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenases had universally underperformed on small noncanonical coenzymes compared to their wild-type (WT) counterparts on natural NAD(P). Here we developed an Iterative (one-site) Mutagenesis and Evolutionary Strategy (IMES) to evolve a flavin-free, NAD-dependent glucose dehydrogenase (GDH) on nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN + ). By integrating rational design, directed evolution, and a novel high-throughput screening method, we obtained the variant M3 (E44H/P191T/V187M). For the first time, an engineered dehydrogenase achieved catalytic efficiencies with NMN + that surpassed those of the WT enzyme with its natural coenzyme NAD + . Specifically, variant M3 exhibited a 3.2-fold higher specific activity and a 2.06-fold greater catalytic efficiency ( k cat / K m ) with NMN + than the WT GDH with NAD + . Furthermore, we established functional NMN-recycling cascades by coupling the NMNH-generating M3 variant with four NMNH-consuming redox enzymes, including flavin-free alcohol dehydrogenase and mannitol dehydrogenase, as well as two flavin-dependent enzymes (i.e., an oxidase and a transhydrogenase). This study establishes an NMN-based cascade redox system applicable to both in vitro biocatalysis and in vivo bioorthogonal chemistry. Replacing NAD with the smaller, lower-cost NMN coenzyme greatly reduced the economic burden of cofactor supply, paving the way for more efficient and cost-effective enzymatic biocatalysis.
items.authors: Zhihua Nie, Zhan Song, Zhenyu Zhai, Yi-Heng P. Job Zhang

items.title: An Affinity-Based Model for Competitive Surfactant Adsorption in Microemulsions
items.abstract: Mixtures of different surfactants are widely employed in microemulsions to tune aggregate stability, selectivity for solute incorporation (as part of separations), and phase behavior. Yet predicting how competing surfactants partition between the aggregate surface and the bulk medium remains an unsolved challenge. We introduce the affinity , a size-independent measure of polar-core coverage that is well-defined across polydisperse aggregates, and derive an affinity-based competitive Langmuir model from the grand canonical partition function. For TODGA/TBP in n-dodecane the model yields ΔΔGads. = -0.84 ± 0.04 kcal/mol favoring TBP and partitions it into an energetic term of -1.10 ± 0.04 kcal/mol and an entropic term of -0.84 ± 0.13 cal/mol K, the latter obtained from single-component simulations alone.
items.authors: Jackson Elowitt, Swarup Banerjee, Aurora E. Clark

items.title: Harnessing Machine Learning and Composite Quantum Chemical Methods for Computing Accurate Bond Dissociation Energies of PFAS
items.abstract: Designing efficient degradation pathways for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) requires access to accurate bond dissociation energies (BDEs). Composite quantum chemical methods such as G4 provide high accuracy ( 1 kcal mol–1) but are limited to small molecules. Density functional theory (DFT) can handle larger systems, but its results vary significantly with the choice of functional and basis set, raising concerns about reliability. Fragment-based methods like the connectivity-based hierarchy (CBH) and its modified form (mCBH) offer G4-level accuracy at DFT cost, but only when using large fragments. Since obtaining G4 energies for large fragments is computationally demanding, these methods are not practical for building large BDE databases. To address this limitation, we introduce a machine learning (ML)-enhanced CBH approach. Here, a regression model is trained on G4-calculated energies of small fragments and is used to predict PFAS BDEs. This strategy achieves near-G4 accuracy without requiring G4 calculations on large fragments. Across diverse PFAS with varying chain lengths and functional groups, our ML-augmented fragmentation-based methods either match or outperform the accuracy of both the mCBH-3 and CBH-3 approaches (both of which require larger fragments), demonstrating that chemical accuracy can be achieved with smaller fragments. By integrating fragment-level quantum data with ML, this hybrid framework provides an efficient pathway for generating reliable BDE datasets and accelerating the discovery of effective PFAS degradation strategies.
items.authors: Kalpak Ghosh, Samir Kumar Nayak, Rohit Batra, Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala

items.title: Decoupling the Thermal Service Limit from Degradability in 3D Printable Covalent Adaptable Networks via Nanohybridization
items.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) represent a critical advancement in sustainable polymers, yet their deployment is frequently constrained by a trade-off between high thermal service limit and on-demand degradability. Herein, we report an organic-inorganic hybrid polymer architecture that decouples thermomechanical robustness from chemical responsiveness. By integrating rigid polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (AcryloPOSS) nanoclusters into a dynamic lipoic acid-based CAN-type matrix, the POSS cages function as steric nanoscale shields that restrict polymer chain mobility. This structural confinement yields a high activation energy for disulfide exchange (204.9 ± 22.5 kJ mol-1), thereby suppressing macroscopic creep and maintaining network integrity up to 250°C, matching the performance of non-degradable commercial thermosets. Furthermore, the hybrid network exhibits chemical stability over a wide pH range yet undergoes complete dissolution in highly alkaline solutions within 24 hours, decomposing into the building blocks of the hybrid polymer. Utilizing digital light processing 3D printing, we demonstrate a dual-curing strategy to fabricate geometrically complex, high-resolution polymeric objects that balance exceptional durability with closed-loop end-of-life deconstructability.
items.authors: Natanel Jarach, Yael Shenhar, Hanna Dodiuk, Samuel Kenig, Shlomo Magdassi

items.title: Fundamental Determinants of Misranking in Affinity-Based Ligand Ranking
items.abstract: Affinity-based prioritization depends on preserving the relative order of ligands, which is distinct from determining each equilibrium dissociation constant, K d , accurately. Errors that substantially bias individual K d values do not necessarily alter ranking if they affect ligands similarly, whereas smaller differential errors can reverse the order of ligands whose true affinities are close. Here, we establish a quantitative framework for understanding this distinction in full-titration binding assays. First-principles analysis of equilibrium 1:1 binding shows that the target-to-affinity ratio, T 0 / K d , governs the amplification of concentration errors into fitted-affinity errors, while the true affinity ratio between two ligands defines the margin that differential errors must overcome to produce rank inversion. Controlled end-to-end simulations extend this analysis to additive and nonadditive response models and map the regimes in which affinity ranking becomes vulnerable. The results show that ranking progressively destabilizes as local affinity separation decreases and T 0 / K d increases. They further demonstrate that ligand-specific signal nonadditivity can introduce differential distortions that impair ranking even when concentration-dependent error amplification is weak, whereas response transformations shared across ligands have substantially less effect on their relative ranking. Library-scale simulations additionally show that strong overall rank correlation can coexist with substantial errors in recovering the highest-affinity candidates, indicating that global rank statistics alone may not adequately assess prioritization performance. We translate these findings into a practical workflow emphasizing appropriate concentration design, validation of response additivity, control of ligand-to-ligand variability, and selection-focused performance metrics for reliable affinity ranking.
items.authors: Tong Ye Wang, Parmeetpal Dhillon, Sergey N. Krylov

items.title: Multi-Step Oxygen Redox Mechanism in the Polyanionic Lithium-Rich Cathode Li2FeSiO4
items.abstract: Lithium-rich cathode materials offer significantly higher energy densities than conventional cathode materials, due to their ability to store charge beyond the formal transition-metal redox limit, via so-called "oxygen redox". In lithium-rich oxides, oxygen redox is accompanied by molecular O 2 formation and transition-metal migration, associated with irreversible structural change and poor cycling stability. Lithium-rich silicates provide an alternative lithium-rich chemistry, and have been proposed to be resilient to O 2 formation at the top of charge, due to their covalently bonded [SiO 4 ]4- framework. We report a computational study of the top-of-charge behaviour of the prototypical silicate cathode Li 2 FeSiO 4 . Using density functional theory, we predict that fully delithiated FeSiO 4 is thermodynamically unstable with respect to oxidation of oxide ions to form molecular O 2 within the bulk material. Ab initio molecular dynamics shows this decomposition occurs spontaneously, via a multi-step mechanism involving Fe(IV) migration and disproportionation to Fe(III) and Fe(V), and subsequent Fe(V) reduction alongside molecular O 2 formation. Our findings demonstrate that polyanionic frameworks do not inherently prevent O 2 formation in lithium-rich cathodes, and illustrate how different previously proposed oxygen redox mechanisms can function as steps within a compound process.
items.authors: Patrick J Taylor, Kit McColl, M Saiful Islam, Benjamin J Morgan

items.title: The first approach to highly substituted dihydroimidazotriazolones and their controlled post-transformations
items.abstract: A novel class of azido-modified α , β -unsaturated Ugi adducts (enamides) has been explored as a versatile platform for post -Ugi transformations. While intramolecular azide-alkyne cycloadditions of Ugi-derived peptidomimetics have been extensively studied, the corresponding azide-alkene cycloadditions on similar scaffolds have remained unexplored. In this work, we report a systematic investigation of intramolecular azide-alkene cycloaddition involving activated enamide moieties derived from Ugi adducts. Enamides readily undergo catalyst-free intramolecular [3+2] cycloaddition under mild conditions to afford the previously unknown 3,3a,4-trisubstituted-3a,4-dihydro-3 H -imidazo[1,2-c][1,2,3]triazol-5(6 H )-one scaffold in high yields. This novel fused heterocyclic system was fully characterised and proved to be a highly versatile intermediate for divergent post -Ugi transformations. Fused dihydrotriazoles transformed into 3,5-dihydroimidazol-4-ones via an elimination of N 2 supplemented by acylamide migration. Additionally, base- or acid-mediated cascades enabled efficient one-pot access to aromatised 1,2,3-triazoles and open-chain triamides, respectively. In total, 4 generations of structural isomers and 2 other classes of compounds were involved in the work. The methodologies developed highlight the synthetic value of azido-modified enamides as divergent intermediates, providing rapid and controlled entry to structurally diverse nitrogen-rich heterocycles and peptidomimetics from simple Ugi adducts derived from α , β- unsaturated aldehydes.
items.authors: Vladyslav Vereshchak, Viacheslav Saraiev, Vladimir Musatov, Svitlana Shishkina, Valentyn Chebanov, Alexander Tsygankov

items.title: Broadly Accessible and Highly Active Hydrophosphination Catalysis with Simple Calcium Compounds in DMSO Solution
items.abstract: Highly earth-abundant and simple calcium precatalysts are reported that address the long-standing challenge of broad scope in hydrophosphination catalysis. With more than 120 examples of hydrophosphination reactions, calcium catalysts are the broadest in scope, including traditional styrene substrates and activated alkenes (Michael acceptors), conjugated dienes, heterocumulenes, alkynes, unactivated alkenes, and even naturally occurring alkenes. Reactions are optimized to maximum conversion, and few examples have less than 90% conversion, making these the most active catalysts to date. Two features contribute to this exceptional scope and activity. The first feature is solvent. Reactions run in DMSO experience a step up in relative rate compared to those in lower-dielectric solvents. Second, more challenging substrates are readily accessed under photocatalytic conditions, a feature already established for calcium precatalysts. The simple precatalyst, Ca(HMDS) 2 (THF) 2 (HMDS = – N(SiMe 3 ) 2 , 1 ), works for all reactions described, and mechanistic evidence points to a nucleophilic attack for amenable substrates. This work highlights critical advances in hydrophosphination (solvent effects, s-block catalysts, and photocatalysis) to yield an abundant metal (calcium) in green solvent with low energy input to achieve hydrophosphination of the widest scope of substrates under operationally simple conditions.
items.authors: Moniruzzaman Moniruzzaman, Rory Waterman

items.title: Structural and Spectroscopic Characterization of Self-Sufficient Cytochrome P450 Fusion Enzymes: CYP102A1 and CYP116B
items.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) monooxygenases are heme-thiolate enzymes that catalyze diverse oxidative transformations essential to metabolism, detoxification, and biosynthesis. While most CYPs rely on separate redox partner proteins for electron delivery, a subset-known as self-sufficient or fusion P450s-incorporate the reductase domain(s) directly within a single polypeptide, enabling efficient intramolecular electron transfer and, in some cases, exceptionally high catalytic turnover. This review examines two representative self-sufficient P450 systems, CYP102A1 (P450 BM3) and CYP116B, summarizing spectroscopic evidence (UV-Vis, EPR, and resonance Raman), supported by available crystal structures, to compare how their distinct domain architectures shape heme electronic structure and catalytic mechanism. CYP102A1, a fused FAD/FMN-heme flavocytochrome from Bacillus megaterium, undergoes pronounced substrate-induced conformational rearrangement and low-spin/highspin switching, properties that are further tunable through active-site mutagenesis (e.g., A82F, F87V, F393 variants) and that underlie its status as the most extensively studied and engineered P450 scaffold. In contrast, CYP116B enzymes, which transfer electrons through a defined FMN-[2Fe–2S]-heme pathway, maintain a comparatively rigid, conserved low-spin heme environment that is less dynamically coupled to substrate binding, although engineered variants (e.g., CYP116B5-SOX) demonstrate their potential for peroxide-driven biocatalysis. Together, these comparisons illustrate how differences in fusion architecture translate into distinct strategies for electron transfer and catalytic control, offering complementary design principlesstructural plasticity in BM3 versus a stable redox scaffold in CYP116B-for engineering nextgeneration self-sufficient P450 biocatalysts.
items.authors: Sravya Vungarala, Mason Daras, Yasmine Elshoweikh, Yilin Liu

items.title: Clearing a benchmark's resolution limit is necessary and not sufficient: measured floors for structure-based virtual screening, and five interventions on a second target
items.abstract: A virtual screening improvement is normally reported as a difference in AUROC between two protocols, each run once, on one benchmark. Two questions are almost never asked: whether the benchmark can resolve a difference of that size, and whether the difference survives a second target. We ask both, and the answers are not the same. The resolution is measurable and predictable. Fifteen replicates of an identical AutoDock Vina protocol on a 755-compound SARS-CoV-2 Mpro panel, varying only --seed, give an AUROC standard deviation of 0.00441 and a one-sided 95% chi-squared bound of 0.00644. Twelve replicates on an 886-compound Factor Xa panel give 0.00682. AUROC variance scales as 1/n, verified within a target (755 to 339 compounds, ratio 1.14) and, on a prediction fixed in advance, across targets (0.00459 predicted, 0.00427 measured, ratio 0.93). A floor can therefore be quoted for a panel that has not been re-measured. It is specific to the method, the protocol and the panel, and borrowing is expensive. Three substitutions we made and corrected cost factors of 4.0 (one method's floor used for another), 2.2 (the sd of a residual charged against a margin), and 1.5 (a floor moved between panel sizes). The floor is only weakly specific to the AUROC level: across simulated panels from 0.28 to 0.90 it varies by 12%, so a floor measured where a method performs poorly is conservative elsewhere. The metric matters more than any of it. On the same replicates, EF@1% has a coefficient of variation 8.6 times AUROC's: a floor of 0.38 against a mean of 2.28, and a third of the value on a smaller panel. Enrichment at an early cutoff is what screening papers usually report, and it is the quantity a benchmark of this size resolves worst. BEDROC (alpha = 20) sits between the two. Clearing the floor does not make a result real, and that is the paper's central claim. Of five interventions measured on Mpro, three clear the floor by wide margins. Re-measured on a second target, none of the four testable ones replicates. The largest (replacing the scoring function on identical poses: +0.140 on Mpro, twenty-two times that panel's floor, with its whole 95% interval above it) comes back at -0.058 on Factor Xa: a reversal of sign, with the interval clear of that target's own floor. Of the two mid-sized effects, one falls to about a quarter of its Mpro value and one changes sign; neither is resolvable. The smallest effect reproduces almost exactly (+0.0082 against +0.0096) and is unresolvable on both. A resolution limit is a necessary filter and a poor certificate. We recommend measuring it, reporting it with its panel size, and treating a result that clears it as eligible for belief rather than established. VERSION NOTE Supersedes v2. The two resolution limits reported in v2 measured the wrong quantity -- one was implementation variance between two scoring-function builds, the other an intervention effect used as its own threshold -- and they were the decision rule for every intervention in that version. They are replaced by seed replication of an unchanged protocol. Four interventions are additionally re-measured on a second target: none replicates, and the largest (+0.140 on Mpro) reverses sign to -0.058 on Factor Xa. A mechanistic explanation offered for that reversal was tested and withdrawn as inconclusive.
items.authors: John Goodman

items.title: Understanding the steric demand of the reactions of nickel(0) complexes with aryl halide substrates
items.abstract: Nickel complexes are able to undergo reactions with organohalides by a variety of fundamental steps, which can be either one-electron or two-electron in nature. Two electron processes are typically some flavour of oxidative addition (OA), but various mechanisms have been proposed for the one-electron reactions, including inner-sphere halogen atom abstraction (HAA) and outer-sphere single electron transfer (SET). It was recently proposed that the steric bulk of a substrate can be used as an indicator of whether HAA is feasible, and therefore that SET was in operation for a specific and bulky substrate. However, the steric requirements for HAA by nickel have not yet been systematically assessed. Here we report a structured assessment of how HAA feasibility might vary with ligand and substrate steric impact. We find that HAA by [Ni(PMe 3 ) 3 ] is feasible even for sterically very hindered substrates. Systems with ferrocene-derived bisphosphine ligands tend to prefer HAA when the ligand and/or the substrate are very sterically bulky.
items.authors: Risnita Vicky Listyarini, Ryan Oliver, Hio U. Lao, David J. Nelson

items.title: Active Atom Identification for Information-Dense Training of Machine-Learning Potentials in Catalysis
items.abstract: Machine-learning potentials (MLPs) extend atomistic simulations beyond the size and time scales accessible to density functional theory while retaining near-first-principles accuracy. However, their reliability depends on training data that cover the relevant potential-energy surface (PES). In heterogeneous catalysis, local changes at active sites may be obscured by redundant nonactive atoms when configurations are selected using global metrics. This limitation calls for an atom-resolved criterion for identifying where chemically relevant configurational information is concentrated. Here we introduce Active Atom Identification (AAI), an algorithm that measures local structural evolution and identifies active atoms that contribute most to configurational diversity. Building on this atom-resolved information, we develop IDEAL (Information-Dense Extraction and Adaptive Learning), which integrates data generation, active-learning selection and dataset refinement into a unified workflow for MLP construction. For CO2 adsorption at Ag/H2O interfaces, a model trained on an IDEAL-selected subset comprising 44% of the original dataset, reaches the accuracy of the full-dataset model. The broad applicability of IDEAL is further demonstrated in two additional applications: database refinement for solid-state electrolytes and transfer learning between zeolite-supported Rh clusters and their hydroxylated analogues. These results validate local structural evolution as an effective criterion for constructing information-dense MLP datasets in complex atomistic systems.
items.authors: Haobo Zhao, Xiongwei Tian, Jixuan Lin, Yuqun Zhuo, Yiming Lu, Hai Xiao

items.title: StateFlux: DFT-Validated Quantum Reactivity across Predicted Metabolic State Networks Shows Limited Incremental Value for Broad Toxicity Prediction
items.abstract: Mechanistic molecular representations are increasingly used to supplement parent structure with protonation, metabolism, and quantum-chemical reactivity, but added physical detail does not necessarily provide predictive information beyond structure. StateFlux represents each drug as a network of chemical and predicted metabolic states with node-level GFN2-xTB properties and edge-resolved changes in ionization potential, electron affinity, electrophilicity, solvation, and local reactivity. On a locked DILIrank 2.0 development set (n = 376; 156 positive and 220 negative), 10 × 5 scaffold-grouped validation gave AUROC/AUPRC values of 0.8249/0.7727 for ECFP, 0.8049/0.7430 for ECFP + FluxCore, and 0.8010/0.7261 for ECFP + StateFluxCore. Strict temporal and scaffold-novel tests showed no consistent gain, and an independent 5,367-compound genotoxicity transfer benchmark reproduced the pattern (AUROC 0.7765 for ECFP versus 0.7732 for StateFluxCore). To separate limited predictive utility from inaccurate low-cost quantum chemistry, 24 parent-to-metabolite transformations were evaluated with 144 ωB97X-D/6-31+G*/SMD single-point calculations. GFN2-xTB closely tracked DFT changes in electrophilicity (Pearson r = 0.963; MAE = 0.408 eV; 79.2% sign agreement). Thus, transformation-induced quantum reactivity can be consistent with higher-level DFT without providing reliable incremental information for broad toxicity classification. Quantum-chemical fidelity and predictive utility should therefore be evaluated as separate claims in chemical machine learning.
items.authors: Aris Tsai

items.title: Prediction of organic additive-induced rheological enhancement of CTAB solutions using machine learning methods
items.abstract: Various organic additives can induce structural rearrangement of surfactant micelles in aqueous solutions, leading to enhanced rheological properties, namely an increase in viscosity, appearance of viscoelasticity, and non-Newtonian behavior. This phenomenon can be exploited in several industries to obtain strong gels. The selection of proper additives and their concentrations remains largely empirical owing to the high number of factors influencing structural rearrangement. This paper aims to employ machine learning (ML) methods to predict whether an enhancement of rheological behavior will occur in cetyltrimethylammonium bromide solutions (CTAB) upon addition of an organic compound. Five different shallow ML algorithms were tested along with graph neural networks (GNNs), using a dataset of 605 data points collected from the literature. Two types of descriptors (RDKit and PaDEL) were applied. Shallow ML algorithms achieved a maximum precision of 0.85 under cross-validation with a random fold split, and this performance did not deteriorate significantly when a structure-based split was applied (0.82). The random forest algorithm was selected based on its comparatively stable performance. GNN achieved a precision of 0.85 (random split) and 0.80 (structure-based split). Analysis of relative contribution of system properties and molecular features to the predictions of shallow and GNN models is consistent with the known physicochemical basis. Experimental validation of ML methods on four prospective compounds unseen during training was carried out. Comparison with ML predictions demonstrated that both models can correctly identify compounds that promote rheological enhancement, but tend to overpredict positive outcomes. However, this drawback may be partially mitigated by applying a pessimistic consensus, and then the accuracy of 0.84 and the precision of 0.73 are achieved for evaluation on the experimental dataset. The present work demonstrates that ML methods can be applied to address the problem of surfactant self-aggregation in solution upon addition of organic additives with room remaining for performance improvement.
items.authors: Timur Yunusov

items.title: Reinterpreting Simulation Results for New Materials Applications with a Large Language Model
items.abstract: In materials discovery, computational results generated for one application may retain value for deciding what to investigate next. Here we use a large language model to reinterpret archived adsorption calculations in the context of framework chemistry and pore structure across three metal–organic framework case studies. Xenon affinity directly guided Xe/Kr selection, while dilute-limit methane affinity transferred more effectively than finite-pressure uptake. We then asked whether archived results could suggest new applications without a predefined target. CO2 results prompted four separation directions, CO2/N2, CO2/CH4, C2H2/CO2, and C2H6/CO2, none of which was recovered when the same materials lacked the archived CO2 information. Nine of 15 CO2-informed material–application pairs ranked in the top quarter of corresponding classical screening distributions. Archived simulations can therefore guide what to investigate next, from selecting materials for a known target to opening a new application.
items.authors: Jihan Kim

items.title: Volcanic ash: a broad-scope natural pesticide for global utilization in agriculture
items.abstract: Overabundant volcanic dust, in the form of volcanic ash or micronized volcanic rock, is a broad-scope natural pesticide. Its physical mechanism of action is chiefly based on adhesion of cuticle and death induction via dehydration, thereby ensuring lack of ecological toxicity. After decades of modest scholarly and industrial interest following the 1972 discovery of the insecticidal mechanism of action of volcanic ash, the first volcanic rock-based pest control formulations were commercialized in Europe in the early 2020s. Applied in agriculture, volcanic dust acts as pesticide, fertilizer, biostimulant and soil conditioner supporting its widespread utilization both by farmers living nearby active volcanoes and basalt quarries and by others in regions where volcanic ash or micronized volcanic rock will be regularly shipped.
items.authors: Mario Pagliaro, Giovanna Li Petri, Giuseppe Angellotti, Rosaria Ciriminna

items.title: Vapor Pressure of Octafluorocyclobutane (RC-318) from 234 K to 387 K Measured with a Variable-Volume View Cell
items.abstract: Saturated vapor pressures of octafluorocyclobutane (c-C4F8, RC-318) were measured at 32 temperatures from 234.33 K to 387.01 K, corresponding to pressures from 20.62 kPa to 2.698 MPa. Measurements were performed in a variable-volume cell with sapphire windows, enabling direct observation of the vapor–liquid meniscus and visual confirmation of the two-phase state at each point. The highest measurement was obtained 1.36 K below the reported critical temperature (Tc = 388.37 K). Temperature was measured with a platinum resistance thermometer traceable to the ITS-90, and pressure was measured with a calibrated transducer. The combined expanded uncertainty in the saturation pressure, U(ps) (k = 2), was estimated to be 0.2–0.6% over the measured range. The data were correlated with a four-term Wagner equation constrained to the critical parameters of Douslin et al.,[3] giving an average absolute relative deviation (AARD) of 0.23%, a root-mean-square relative deviation of 0.34%, and a maximum absolute relative deviation of 0.82%. The measurements agree with the reference equation of state of Platzer et al.[28] with an AARD of 0.27%. Combined with saturated-phase molar volumes from the reference equation of state, the correlation gives an enthalpy of vaporization that decreases from about 25.4 kJ·mol−1 at 234 K, through 23.3 kJ·mol−1 at the normal boiling point, and approaches zero at the critical point. These measurements provide a modern, internally consistent vapor-pressure data set for a high-GWP fluorinated gas that is widely used in semiconductor processing and has also been investigated for dielectric applications.
items.authors: Jae Uk Yoon, Jin Woo Bae

items.title: Lithium-Lithium Correlations and the Emergence of Transport Properties in Solvate Ionic Liquid Electrolytes
items.abstract: Solvate ionic liquids (SILs), equimolar mixtures of lithium salts and chelating glymes, are promising electrolytes for energy storage due to their high thermal stability and low vapor pressure. However, the low lithium transference numbers and modest ionic conductivities of SILs limit device performance. Here, long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations combined with transport characterization identify the Li+-Li+ structural decorrelation as the key descriptor governing ion transport in SILs composed of lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and glymes of various lengths. These SILs have extended ionic networks in which anions bridge multiple Li+ centers, generating long-lived structural correlations. SIL ion transport is initiated by speciation exchange, which disrupts the ionic network and leads to structural decorrelation on nanosecond timescales. Decreasing glyme chain length increases anion bridging, slows structural decorrelation, and decreases ionic conductivity, while increasing lithium transference. These results establish structural decorrelation as a key descriptor of transport in SILs. While the anion-mediated decorrelation is demonstrated for SILs, this framework is general and can be applied to any high concentration electrolyte in which transport emerges from the reorganization of correlated ionic networks.
items.authors: Daniel G. Kuroda, Orlando Carrillo-Bohórquez, Revati Kumar

items.title: Decoding Residue-level Energetic Rewiring in PROTAC Ternary Cooperativity
items.abstract: Binding cooperativity is a defining determinant of the stability, selectivity, and degradation efficiency of PROTAC-mediated ternary complexes, yet its molecular origin remains poorly understood because existing computational approaches largely provide only global affinity estimates. Here we present MASIC (Multimeric Alanine Scanning with Interaction Convolution), a thermodynamically grounded end-point free energy framework that enables quantitative residue-level analysis of cooperativity in multimeric protein-protein-PROTAC systems. MASIC establishes a unified formulation linking end-point free energy theory, alanine-scanning interaction entropy, and multimeric cooperativity, while introducing a statistically robust interaction-convolution strategy that overcomes the finite-sampling instability of conventional interaction-entropy estimators. Beyond quantifying overall cooperativity, MASIC provides, to our knowledge, the first residue-resolved cooperativity landscapes of PROTAC ternary complexes and introduces the concept of cooperativity hotspots, identifying residues that govern cooperative stabilization rather than binding affinity alone. Extensive validation across diverse experimentally characterized PROTAC systems, including BRD9-VHL, BRD4-CRBN and FKBP12-CRBN, demonstrates accurate prediction of experimental cooperativity and consistently outperforms established structure-based approaches. Residue-level analyses reveal previously inaccessible many-body interaction networks underlying synergistic and antagonistic cooperativity, providing mechanistic insight into ternary-complex formation. Together, MASIC establishes a general framework for dissecting cooperative molecular recognition in multimeric biomolecular assemblies and provides a foundation for the rational design of next-generation targeted protein degraders.
items.authors: Wenjing Zhou, Xiaohui Wang, Lizhen Huo, Yucheng Han, Lingjie Kong, Baochuan Hu

items.title: Programmable Oxidation in Flow on Interdigitated Lateral Catalytic Condensers
items.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis remains fundamentally limited by the intrinsic static electronic and physical structure of the catalyst surface during reaction that restricts catalytic rates and limits reactions to equilibrium. To circumvent these limitations, a catalytic condenser enables the non-Faradaic dynamic modulation of surface binding energies through an external potential. Here, we describe an interdigitated (IDT) internal ion gel catalytic condenser within a continuous flow reactor for the electronic control of thermochemical carbon monoxide oxidation on Pt active sites. The device utilizes a thermally stable, high-capacitance ion gel electrolyte (PA6,6/[EDMIM][TFSI]) to establish an electric double layer at the metal-electrolyte interface, enabling both charge condensation and a strong electric field at the Pt active sites. Field strength was measured by Stark tuning of 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (4-MBN) on a model Ag electrode, with field strengths on the order of ~1 V nm -1 shifting a voltage-dependent nitrile response up to ~4 cm -1 /V at negative applied potential. By applying a bias of ±1 V at 180°C, the device both increases and decreases the catalytic turnover frequency of CO oxidation. These results support surface-charge modulation as the origin of catalytic rate enhancement for the non-Faradaic dynamic tuning of thermochemical reaction rates.
items.authors: Ruixue Xiong, Wonwoo Lee, Chaehoon Kim, Justin Hopkins, Jesse Canavan, Jaeheon Kim

items.title: Asymmetric Anti-Hydrogenation of Tetrasubstituted Alkenes
items.abstract: Asymmetric alkene hydrogenation is a foundational method for constructing chiral molecules, with broad applications in pharmaceutical synthesis, natural-product synthesis and materials science. However, the stereochemical outcomes accessible through conventional asymmetric hydrogenation are constrained by its underlying mechanism. Established catalysts, including complexes of iridium, rhodium, ruthenium and platinum, typically deliver both hydrogen atoms to the same face of an alkene to give syn-hydrogenation products. The complementary process, in which hydrogen atoms are stereoselectively delivered from opposite alkene faces, would provide direct access to complementary stereochemical products, but remains poorly developed. Here we show that engineered heme proteins catalyze asymmetric anti-hydrogenation of unactivated cyclic tetrasubstituted alkenes. These genetically encoded catalysts operate through a cooperative radical mechanism in which an active-site iron hydride delivers a hydrogen atom to one face of the alkene to generate a transient carbon-centered radical, which is subsequently quenched from the opposite face by a distal cysteine residue. The spatially separated hydrogen-atom donors thereby enable sequential stereodetermining events, furnishing anti-hydrogenated products with high diastereo-
items.authors: Justin Manoff, Kyle Schultz, Julian Morales, Aris V. Rubio, Cesar Torres, Sattwik Chakraborty

items.title: A Crystalline Aminoborane Radical Defines a New Stabilization Strategy and Enables Dihydrogen Activation and Transformation
items.abstract: Borane radical anions are highly reactive open-shell species, yet their application in dihydrogen activation remains rare. Persistent borane radical anions have primarily been accessed through π-conjugation and kinetic protection. Here, we introduce an adaptive stabilization strategy in which a Zr center dynamically adjusts its coordination geometry to stabilize the boron-centered radical or to disengage from the boron center when reactivity is required. This strategy enables access to an aminoborane radical anion and its boron-centered reactivity toward dihydrogen activation and transformation. D2 labeling further confirmed the dihydrogen activation process and demonstrated that the activated hydrogen can be transferred to organic substrates. Theoretical calculations elucidate the adaptive B–Zr orbital interaction responsible for radical stabilization and the mechanism of H2 activation.
items.authors: Leibo Tan, Xiaocui Liu, Junyi Wang, Michael Moos, Ivo Krummenacher, Maik Finze

items.title: Solvent organization and QM–MM nonbonded interactions govern excitation energies of cationic Methylene Blue: a multiscale Dual-MD/ML and QM/MMPol benchmark
items.abstract: Methylene blue (MB) has been utilized as a therapeutic agent and has been in clinical and research use for more than a century. The cationic nature of MB+ and the mutual polarization between solute and solvent constitute not just higher-order corrections but dominant contributions; accordingly, polarizable embedding approaches have been shown to substantially modify computed absorption characteristics of dyes in condensed phases, but it is still a challenge to reproduce the MB+ absorption spectrum. Here, we benchmark three multiscale simulation workflows, differing in force-field parametrization and configurational sampling strategy. In parallel, we evaluate five density-functional approximations to describe the electronic structure and to compute the associated absorption spectra of the solvated system. Consistent with experimental observations, methylene blue exhibits pronounced sensitivity to the local solvation environment, and the results indicate that the Dual-MD protocol is compatible with both conventional Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics (BOMD) and machine-learning (ML)-based potentials. Moreover, upon inclusion of explicit water molecules in the QM region, fully hybrid functionals yield excitation energies in excellent agreement with experiment.
items.authors: Renato D. Cunha, Maurício D. Coutinho-Neto, Paula Homem-de-Mello

items.title: Tafel curvature analysis in electrocatalysis: theoretical foundations and microkinetic simulations
